links.outcome: Hallucination and omission rates in LLM-generated notes across 18 experiments, clinician-annotated by severity
links.effect: Of 12,999 sentences, 191 had hallucinations (1.47%), 84 (44%) major; 1712 of 49,590 transcript sentences omitted (3.45%), 286 (16.7%) major. Iterative refinement cut major omissions from 61 to 0.
links.quote: Of 12,999 sentences in 450 clinical notes, 191 sentences had hallucinations (1.47%), of which 84 sentences (44%) were major (could impact patient diagnosis and management if left uncorrected).

links.outcome: Reference standard via dual clinician annotation with senior clinician adjudication of discrepancies
links.effect: Two clinician reviewers evaluated each note sentence, with consolidation by a senior clinician for discrepancies; the study applied this protocol but did not compare outcomes with or without it.
links.quote: In cases of discrepancy between the two reviewers, consolidation was performed by a senior clinician with over 20 years of clinical experience.

links.outcome: LLM-generated vs clinician-written notes: hallucinations and omissions on same transcripts
links.effect: Clinician-written notes had slightly more hallucinations but fewer omissions than LLM notes (Experiment 17); LLM best configurations had fewer errors per note than reported human rates.
links.quote: Interestingly, findings suggested slightly more hallucinations in clinician-written notes but fewer omissions, highlighting key differences in human vs. LLM-generated note content.

links.outcome: Major hallucinations concentrated in Plan section of generated clinical notes
links.effect: Hallucinations occurred in all sections, most commonly (20%) in the Plan section; negation hallucinations were 30% of hallucinations.
links.quote: Hallucinations occurred in all sections, but most commonly (20%) in the Plan section of the clinical note.

links.outcome: Hallucination and omission rates of generative LLM clinical notes
links.effect: 1.47% hallucination rate and 3.45% omission rate; hallucinations more often major (44%) than omissions (16.7%).
links.quote: Our experiment results show that omissions are more common than hallucinations (3.45% to 1.47%, respectively).

links.outcome: Re-testing errors after prompt and workflow changes to note-generation pipeline
links.effect: Prompt change from Exp 3 to 8 reduced major hallucinations 75% (4 to 1), major omissions 58% (24 to 10); atomisation (Exp 5) increased major hallucinations from 4 to 25, showing changes can degrade safety.
links.quote: The change in the prompt from Experiments 3 to 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75% (from 4 to 1), major omissions by 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions by 35% (114 to 74) (Fig. 8 ).

links.outcome: Effect of prompt/workflow variations on hallucinations and omissions using fixed seed and temperature
links.effect: Structured prompts, function calls, and atomisation changed error counts; function-call iterations eliminated major omissions (61 to 0) and cut minor omissions 58% (130 to 54).
links.quote: As a result of these changes, we eliminated major omissions completely, decreasing them from 61 to 0, and reduced minor omissions by 58%, from 130 to 54.
